title: Harbor Planning Integration Master Roadmap
goal: Make Planning the shared project truth between Harbor One UI, MCP-enabled agents, JSON roadmaps, Raptor Memory and sparse operator notifications.
user_workflow: The user works in the Agent screen or with another AI and develops a plan.
The plan is converted into a validated JSON roadmap through Planning MCP.
The roadmap is stored in the right project directory with a predictable folder structure.
The roadmap is processed into Raptor Memory as derived planning context with provenance.
Harbor One shows one sparse notification that the project roadmaps changed.
Clicking the notification switches to Planning, opens Overview, highlights the new or changed roadmap and expands its summary.
When an AI is asked to work on the roadmap, it retrieves the roadmap plus context pack through MCP.
The AI updates roadmap progress through MCP while working, but routine progress updates stay silent.
Create and delete events notify the operator; delete events remain undoable from the interface.

sub_roadmaps.role: MCP contract for create, read, update, context packs, event classification and gated writes.
Harbor One V2 Planning UI, Overview graph, notification jump target and expanded roadmap summaries.
Canonical lifecycle for derived Raptor Memory entries and provenance without raw private content.
Safe notification boundary; Harbor Planning uses sparse structural events only.
Review and undo surfaces for deletes, gates, uncertain writes and operator decisions.

canonical_project_structure.principle: JSON roadmaps are the planning source of truth. Markdown is a rendered view or handoff only.
notes: Roadmap files may be stored under docs/plans while the service is repo-only, but the logical project layout should already appear in metadata.
Project, roadmap, gate, todo and event IDs must be stable enough for UI deep links and MCP context packs.
Delete operations must create undo metadata before removing or hiding the target.

notification_policy.principle: Planning MCP is infrastructure, not a notification stream.
ui_behavior: Notifications appear in the Harbor header bell, not as modal interruptions.
Clicking a planning notification opens the Planning workspace, focuses Overview and highlights the referenced roadmap or gate.
A notification may expand the roadmap rectangle to show the short summary and source metadata.
Routine MCP calls must not create visible notifications.

graph_rules: Every visible line is an edge to a Roadmap or Gate node.
The edge color follows the target node state.
Roadmap rectangles show only the roadmap designation while collapsed.
Expanded roadmap rectangles show a short full-roadmap summary.
Only gates that block progress between roadmaps are visible in Overview.
Hovering a gate dims unrelated nodes and highlights the affected roadmaps and direct gate edges.

visible_in_frontpage_v2: Planning workspace with Projects, Overview and Roadmaps windows.
Roadmap list and graph selection highlight each other.
Roadmap selection opens a Document Viewer-style roadmap document.
Roadmap document has a readable mode with summary, tasks and gates plus a Data mode for JSON.
Spark buttons can send the full roadmap or a roadmap section to the Agent composer as a pinned context bubble.
Spark switches the active workspace to Agent and focuses the composer.
prototype_boundaries: Roadmap Viewer content is derived from static demo graph data, not from real project JSON files.
Editable fields are UI-only and do not persist through Planning MCP yet.
Spark currently creates frontend context bubbles only; it does not yet request a service-backed context pack.
Roadmap document JSON is a rendered draft view, not yet validated or written back as planning truth.
Selection-to-document behavior is implemented for visible roadmap demo nodes only.
No Playwright regression flow exists yet for list selection, graph selection, viewer opening or Spark handoff.

open_integration_gaps.summary: Replace static V2 roadmap demo data with service-backed project and roadmap JSON payloads.
Persist Roadmap Document Viewer edits through validated Planning MCP draft or patch flow.
Turn Spark from frontend context bubble creation into a service-backed context-pack handoff.
Let sparse Planning notifications open Overview, highlight the changed roadmap and optionally open its document viewer.
Add Playwright coverage for roadmap selection, viewer opening, edit affordances and Spark handoff.

mcp_contract_requirements: Agents must load roadmap and context pack before executing roadmap work.
Roadmap creation writes must validate JSON schema and record source refs.
Roadmap progress updates should be audit logged but silent in the Harbor UI.
Roadmap creation/deletion emits a sparse notification event.
Deletion returns undo metadata and never becomes irreversible without an operator-visible recovery path.
Context packs may include Raptor Memory summaries and provenance, but not raw private content.

slice_queue.objective: Create the master roadmap that connects UI, MCP, project storage, Raptor Memory and sparse notifications.
slice_queue.done_when: The master roadmap exists as valid JSON and points to the relevant sub-roadmaps.

slice_queue.objective: Define the canonical project folder and JSON schema contract for project, roadmap, gate, todo, event and memory index files.
slice_queue.done_when: The contract explains IDs, folder layout, JSON object roles, migration from docs/plans and undo metadata.

slice_queue.objective: Extend Planning MCP service payloads with event classification: silent update versus operator notification.
slice_queue.done_when: Create/delete/gate-decision events are classified for notification while routine progress and context reads remain silent.

slice_queue.objective: Process validated roadmaps into derived Raptor Memory planning context with provenance and no raw private content.
slice_queue.done_when: Roadmap summaries, gates and source refs become rebuildable derived memory entries with stable references.

slice_queue.objective: Create a safe notification payload shape for Planning changes that deep-links into Harbor One Planning Overview.
slice_queue.done_when: Planning notifications contain project_id, roadmap_id or gate_id, severity, reason and UI target without secrets or raw private content.

slice_queue.objective: Implement Harbor V2 behavior for notification click -> Planning Overview -> highlighted expanded roadmap summary.
slice_queue.done_when: Clicking a sample notification switches to Planning, focuses Overview and expands/highlights the referenced roadmap.

slice_queue.objective: Define the user-visible undo flow for roadmap/project deletion without making every routine update noisy.
slice_queue.done_when: Delete notifications and undo controls are clear, reversible and sparse.

slice_queue.objective: Replace static V2 roadmap demo data with a bounded Planning service payload that feeds Overview, Roadmaps list and Roadmap Document Viewer from the same project JSON source.
slice_queue.backend_boundary: PMCP-5b may complete the bounded document payload independently; this HPIM slice remains open until the V2 graph/list/viewer UI consumes it.
slice_queue.done_when: One service-backed roadmap payload drives graph, list and document viewer without duplicating roadmap state in frontend fixtures.

slice_queue.objective: Persist Roadmap Document Viewer edits as validated JSON draft or patch proposals instead of UI-only text changes.
slice_queue.backend_boundary: PMCP-5c may complete validate/draft/diff behavior independently; this HPIM slice remains open until approved V2 editor affordances consume it.
slice_queue.done_when: Summary, task and Data-mode edits validate against the roadmap schema, produce an auditable draft or patch, and cannot silently overwrite conflicting MCP updates.

slice_queue.objective: Upgrade Spark buttons from frontend-only context bubbles to service-backed Agent context handoffs.
slice_queue.backend_boundary: PMCP-5d may complete bounded section context packs and redacted audit metadata independently; this HPIM slice remains open until approved Spark UI behavior consumes them.
slice_queue.done_when: Spark requests a bounded context pack for the selected roadmap or section, pins the returned context to Agent, focuses the composer and records redacted audit metadata.

slice_queue.objective: Extend sparse Planning notification deep links so roadmap-created and roadmap-updated notifications can open Planning, highlight the roadmap and optionally open the Roadmap Document Viewer.
slice_queue.backend_boundary: HPIM-4 and PMCP-6b may complete logical notification candidates and sparse event classification independently; this HPIM slice remains open until approved V2 navigation behavior consumes them.
slice_queue.done_when: A sample notification payload can route to Planning Overview, select the referenced roadmap and open its document view without modal interruption.

slice_queue.objective: Add browser regression coverage for the Planning V2 interactions that are currently prototype-only.
slice_queue.backend_boundary: Backend contract tests may complete independently; this browser slice starts only after the approved UI behaviors exist.
tests: Playwright: roadmap row click opens document viewer
Playwright: graph node click opens document viewer
Playwright: Spark switches to Agent and pins roadmap context
slice_queue.done_when: Focused browser tests cover roadmap list selection, graph selection, document viewer mode switch and Spark-to-Agent context handoff.

gate_queue.decision_needed: Hand the five V2 Planning integration/browser slices to the UI owner and approve their interaction sequence without changing backend contract ownership.
gate_queue.safe_preparation_done: HPIM-1 storage and HPIM-4 notification-candidate contracts are repository-ready. PMCP-5b, PMCP-5c, PMCP-5d and PMCP-6b remain independently completable backend contracts and do not pre-complete these UI slices.
gate_queue.risk_if_bypassed: A backend runner could edit active V2 UI hotfiles, claim UI done from route tests alone or add Playwright coverage before the intended interactions exist.

non_goals: No notification for every Planning MCP tool call.
No raw private content in roadmap memory entries, notifications, audit logs or context packs.
No Markdown source of truth for planning state.
No irreversible delete without undo metadata.
No automatic completion of roadmap work without evidence refs.
verification: Future: focused Planning MCP service tests
Future: Playwright notification deep-link UI check
recommended_next_step: Create HPIM-1 project storage contract, then implement HPIM-2 in the Planning MCP service before wiring the V2 notification deep-link UI.
